## Dropdown Menu (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/dropdown-menu)

Groups, shortcuts, checkbox and radio items, submenus and destructive actions.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/dropdown-menu/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
  DropdownMenuLinkItem,
  DropdownMenuCheckboxItem,
  DropdownMenuRadioGroup,
  DropdownMenuRadioItem,
  DropdownMenuGroup,
  DropdownMenuGroupLabel,
  DropdownMenuSeparator,
  DropdownMenuShortcut,
  DropdownMenuSub,
  DropdownMenuSubTrigger,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Row actions

The most common admin pattern: a "⋯" button per table row.

```tsx
<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label={`Actions for ${order.id}`} />}>
    <MoreHorizontalIcon />
  </DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent align="end">
    <DropdownMenuItem onClick={() => open(order)}>View</DropdownMenuItem>
    <DropdownMenuSeparator />
    <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={() => refund(order)}>Refund</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>
```

## Submenus

Put a `DropdownMenuSubTrigger` and a `DropdownMenuContent` inside `DropdownMenuSub`.

## Accessibility

- Arrow keys move between items, type-ahead jumps to an item, Enter/Space activates, Escape closes.
- `DropdownMenuShortcut` is a visual hint only; register the keyboard shortcut yourself.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['DropdownMenuContent', 'DropdownMenuItem', 'DropdownMenuShortcut']} baseUi="menu" />

## Overlays (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/index)

Layered interface elements that appear above base page content for focused interactions.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Overlays

Overlays present supplementary workflows, context-sensitive details, and decision prompts above the primary page canvas. They enable Northwind Traders operators to complete focused sub-tasks without navigating away from their active workspace.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="components/overlays" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Modality**: Use `Dialog` or `AlertDialog` when operator confirmation or focused data entry is mandatory before proceeding. Use `Sheet` for wide inspection panels and edit drawers.
- **Focus management**: Overlays automatically trap focus when opened, restore focus to the triggering element upon dismissal, and close on Escape key navigation.
- **Progressive disclosure**: Reserve `Tooltip` for non-essential keyboard hints and iconography descriptions. Use `Popover` for rich interactive menus and filters.

## Sheet (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/sheet)

For filters, record details and edit forms next to a list. Slides from any side, RTL-aware.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/sheet/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import {
  Sheet,
  SheetTrigger,
  SheetContent,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetTitle,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetBody,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetClose,
} from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Sheet>
  <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Filters</SheetTrigger>
  <SheetContent side="right">
```

`side` is `right` (default), `left`, `top` or `bottom`. Left and right flip in right-to-left layouts.

Same as [Dialog](/ui/docs/components/overlays/dialog): focus is trapped, Escape closes, and the

## Tooltip (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/components/overlays/tooltip)

Names icon buttons and shows shortcuts. Shared delay across a toolbar.

<ComponentPreview name="overlays/tooltip/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Tooltip, TooltipTrigger, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Tooltip>
  <TooltipTrigger render={<Button iconOnly variant="ghost" aria-label="Archive" />}>
    <ArchiveIcon />
  </TooltipTrigger>
  <TooltipContent>Archive</TooltipContent>
</Tooltip>
```

Wrap your app in `TooltipProvider` once. After the first tooltip opens, moving to the next trigger
shows it instantly, which makes toolbars feel fast.

## Accessibility

- Opens on hover and keyboard focus; Escape closes it.
- Tooltips are not reachable on touch devices and are skipped by some screen readers. The trigger
  still needs its own `aria-label`, and tooltips must never hold essential information.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['TooltipContent', 'TooltipProvider']} baseUi="tooltip" />

## What's in it

This reference example combines our layout and widget components into a responsive HRMS application layout, matching our reference dashboard composition.

| Part                     | Components                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Global Navigation**    | [`AppRail`](/ui/docs/components/layout/app-rail) on the far left with `AppRailItem`                                                                                                                                         |

Open the **Code** tab to copy the full page. The layout responds to its container and viewport widths:

Brand panel, stepper, responsive form grid, locale selects, validation and a wizard footer.

## Colour (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/colour)

OKLCH semantic palette, contrast tokens, and functional roles.

# Colour

The innostes UI design system employs a semantic colour architecture formulated in the OKLCH colour space. OKLCH guarantees perceptual uniformity across shades, ensuring predictable contrast ratios and consistent luminance across light and dark display modes.

## Semantic architecture

Rather than binding visual elements directly to raw hex values, the library exposes functional tokens mapped to operational roles:

- `primary`: Core interactive triggers, selected states, and brand emphasis.
- `secondary`: Supporting interface elements, subtle hover backgrounds, and secondary actions.
- `muted`: Low-emphasis surfaces, disabled borders, and secondary typography.
- `accent`: Interactive callouts, active navigation items, and highlighted records.
- `destructive`: Error banners, irreversible deletions, and critical alert indicators.
- `success`, `warning`, `info`: Contextual status indicators for transactional data tables and badges.

Detailed token swatches, dark mode mappings, and contrast ratio validation tables are maintained in `packages/ui/tailwind/theme.css`.

---

## Dark mode (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/dark-mode)

Dark theme implementation, token inversion, and hydration strategies.

# Dark mode

innostes UI provides native dark mode support across every component, chart, and widget. Theme switching relies on CSS class toggling (`.dark`) or data attributes (`data-theme="dark"`), updating OKLCH token variables without triggering component re-renders.

## Implementation overview

Dark mode tokens are defined in `packages/ui/tailwind/dark.css`. When the `.dark` class is applied to the root `<html>` or container element, CSS custom properties are remapped to appropriate dark-variant values.

In Next.js applications, theme synchronization is managed using `next-themes`, ensuring zero flash of unstyled content (FOUC) during client-side hydration.

---

## Icons (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/icons)

Iconography principles, Lucide icon integration, and accessibility conventions.

# Icons

Icons in innostes UI provide immediate visual cues alongside textual labels. The design system standardises on the Lucide icon library, ensuring consistent stroke weights, optical alignment, and predictable bounding boxes across all components.

## Guidelines

- **Textual accompaniment**: Icons that trigger interactive operations must include visible text or an explicit `aria-label` for assistive technologies.
- **Decorative iconography**: Icons that accompany descriptive text should receive `aria-hidden="true"` to prevent duplicate screen reader announcements.
- **Sizing standards**: Standard icon sizes align with typographic scale: `size-3.5` (14px) for compact tags, `size-4` (16px) for standard buttons and inputs, and `size-5` (20px) for navigation items.

---

## Motion (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/motion)

Transition durations, easing curves, and reduced-motion accessibility.

# Motion

Motion in innostes UI is functional, understated, and swift. Animation serves exclusively to orient operators during spatial state transitions—such as expanding accordion panels, opening dialog overlays, and displaying toast notifications.

## Animation principles

- **Duration**: Micro-interactions complete within 150ms to 200ms. Structural layout changes and large overlay entrances finish within 250ms to prevent perceptible lag.
- **Easing**: Natural decelerate curves (`cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)`) govern entrance animations, whilst accelerate curves govern dismissals.
- **Reduced motion**: Every animated component respects the user's `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` system preference by replacing motion with immediate opacity fades or zero-duration transitions.

---

## Spacing and layout (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/spacing)

4px spatial rhythm, density modes, and responsive layout primitives.

# Spacing and layout

Consistent spatial rhythm prevents visual clutter and establishes structural relationships between interface elements. innostes UI adopts a 4px base increment across padding, margin, gap, and dimension tokens.

## Spatial grid

Spatial values follow a linear 4px progression aligned with standard Tailwind CSS spacing utilities:

- `1` (4px): Micro-spacing between icon glyphs and adjacent inline text.
- `2` (8px): Compact padding inside buttons, badges, and grouped controls.
- `3` (12px): Default internal padding for form inputs and table cells.
- `4` (16px): Card padding, dialog gutters, and standard component gaps.
- `6` (24px) to `8` (32px): Layout section margins and page header separation.

Components accommodate both standard and compact density modes, allowing operators to adjust data density according to screen resolution and task requirements.

---

## Status legend (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/status-legend)

Stability tiers and readiness criteria for components in @innostes/ui.

# Status legend

Every component, widget, and chart in `@innostes/ui` carries an explicit status badge reflecting its API stability and production readiness. These statuses establish clear expectations for application developers across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd.

## Status tiers

### Stable

The component has completed thorough browser QA, unit testing, and accessibility verification. Its public API conforms strictly to Semantic Versioning (SemVer).

- **Breaking changes**: Breaking changes occur only in major version increments (e.g. `1.0.0` to `2.0.0`), accompanied by migration guides and codemods where feasible.
- **Production readiness**: Recommended for all mission-critical production interfaces and customer-facing workflows.
- **Support**: Receives active maintenance, security patches, and forward-compatibility testing across supported React runtimes.

### Beta

The component is functionally complete and usable in production environments, but its API surface may undergo refinements based on enterprise team feedback.

- **Breaking changes**: Breaking modifications may occur in minor version increments (e.g. `0.2.0` to `0.3.0`), with documented migration paths in release notes.
- **Production readiness**: Suitable for early adoption, internal pilot tools, and feature development with active developer oversight.
- **Feedback**: Developers are encouraged to report ergonomics issues and edge cases before the component graduates to Stable.

### Experimental

The component represents an early architectural exploration or prototype. It demonstrates emerging interaction patterns or evaluates new underlying technologies.

- **Breaking changes**: Breaking changes or removal may occur in any release without prior deprecation notices.
- **Production readiness**: Intended strictly for experimentation and design prototyping. Avoid using in core enterprise transactions.

## Graduation criteria

A component graduates from Beta to Stable only when meeting all of the following requirements:

1. **Complete documentation**: Full adherence to the component documentation template, including anatomical breakdown, interactive examples, do/don't guidelines, and keyboard interaction tables.
2. **Automated test coverage**: Unit and integration test suites covering at least 90% statement coverage across all visual variants, states, and accessibility hooks.
3. **Multi-runtime verification**: Verified operational stability across React 19, React 18, and React 17 environments.
4. **Design token conformance**: Full support for both light and dark themes using OKLCH colour tokens and CSS variables.

---

## Typography (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/foundations/typography)

Type scale, font stacks, and typographic hierarchy for enterprise data density.

# Typography

Typographic scale in innostes UI balances high information density with sustained reading comfort. Designed for enterprise data grids, accounting ledgers, and operational dashboards at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd, the typographic hierarchy prioritises tabular alignment and clear legibility.

## Type scale

The type scale maps to CSS custom properties defined in the root stylesheet:

- `text-xs` (12px): Metadata timestamps, badge labels, and compact table captions.
- `text-sm` (14px): Standard enterprise body text, input fields, and data grid cells.
- `text-base` (16px): Document body copy, modal subtitles, and standard card headers.
- `text-lg` to `text-2xl` (18px–24px): Section titles, metric card values, and page headings.

The primary system font stack leverages modern geometric system typefaces with automatic fallback to Inter and Segoe UI, paired with monospace font stacks optimized for tabular numeric data.

---

## Next.js (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/frameworks/nextjs)

Integration guide for Next.js App Router, React Server Components, and styling.

# Next.js

`@innostes/ui` integrates cleanly with Next.js 15 and 16 App Router. Because the library uses modern Base UI primitives with client-side interactive state, components declare `'use client'` where necessary, enabling composition inside React Server Components.

## Setup

Install `@innostes/ui` alongside required styling dependencies:

```bash
npm install @innostes/ui lucide-react clsx tailwind-merge
```

Import the stylesheet in your root layout:

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import '@innostes/ui/styles.css';

export default function RootLayout({
  children,
}: {
  children: React.ReactNode;
}) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>{children}</body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

Components that wrap client events (such as `Button`, `Dialog`, or `Select`) can be imported directly into server components or nested within interactive client wrappers.

---

## Vite (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/frameworks/vite)

Integration guide for Vite React projects with Tailwind CSS.

# Vite

Vite provides a lightning-fast build environment for Single Page Applications (SPAs). `@innostes/ui` ships with pre-bundled ES modules and CSS entry points designed for instant hot-module reloading in Vite.

## Setup

Create or configure your Vite project with React and TypeScript:

```bash
npm install @innostes/ui lucide-react clsx tailwind-merge
```

Include the global stylesheet in your main entry point:

```tsx
// src/main.tsx
import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App';
import '@innostes/ui/styles.css';

ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <App />
  </React.StrictMode>
);
```

When building with Tailwind CSS v4, reference `@innostes/ui/tailwind` in your primary CSS entry to inherit all OKLCH design tokens.

---

## Introduction (https://innostes.com/ui/docs)

Accessible React components for admin interfaces, built on Base UI and Tailwind CSS.

innostes UI is the component library behind every innostes product. It gives you everything an admin
panel needs (forms, tables, dialogs, navigation and an app shell), with one consistent API and
your own theme.

<ComponentPreview name="examples/dashboard" align="start" className="p-0 sm:p-0" />

## Why innostes UI

## Installation (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/installation)

Add innostes UI to a React app in a few minutes.

## Requirements

- React 17, 18 or 19 (and the matching React DOM). The test suite runs on all three.
- Tailwind CSS v4 (optional, recommended)

`@base-ui/react`, `class-variance-authority`, `clsx` and `tailwind-merge` are installed with the package.

<Steps>
<Step>

### Install the package

```bash tab="pnpm"
pnpm add @innostes/ui
```

```bash tab="npm"
npm install @innostes/ui
```

```bash tab="yarn"
yarn add @innostes/ui
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Add the styles

<Tabs items={['With Tailwind CSS', 'Without Tailwind CSS']}>
<Tab value="With Tailwind CSS">

Import the package after Tailwind in your main CSS file. Components then use **your** theme, and
Tailwind only generates the classes the components actually use.

```css title="app/globals.css"
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@innostes/ui/tailwind.css';
@import '@innostes/ui/dark.css'; /* optional dark theme */
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="Without Tailwind CSS">

Import the precompiled stylesheet once, in your app entry.

```ts title="main.tsx"
import '@innostes/ui/styles.css';
import '@innostes/ui/dark.css'; // optional dark theme
```

It uses the default theme and contains no CSS reset, so it won't restyle the rest of your app.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

</Step>
<Step>

### Add the providers

Mount `Toaster` once to show [toasts](/ui/docs/components/feedback/toast), and wrap the app in
`TooltipProvider` so tooltips share their delay.

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import { Toaster, TooltipProvider } from '@innostes/ui';

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <TooltipProvider>{children}</TooltipProvider>
        <Toaster />
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

Popups render in a portal at the end of `<body>`. If your root element creates its own stacking
context, add `isolation: isolate` to it so popups always appear on top.

</Step>
<Step>

### Use a component

```tsx
import { Button, toast } from '@innostes/ui';

export function SaveButton() {
  return <Button onClick={() => toast.success('Saved')}>Save</Button>;
}
```

</Step>
</Steps>

## Next.js

Interactive components ship with `"use client"`, so you can import them straight into Server
Components. Helpers like `cn()` and `buttonVariants()` work on the server too.

## TypeScript

Types ship with the package. Every prop has TSDoc, so your editor shows descriptions and defaults
on hover.

## Application shell (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/app-shell)

Composable layout scaffolding for multi-tenant enterprise dashboards.

# Application shell

The application shell provides the structural frame within which ERP modules operate. Comprising `AppRail`, `Sidebar`, `TopBar`, and `PageHeader`, it maintains continuous context, breadcrumb paths, and user account actions.

## Structure

1. **Primary rail**: High-level module switching (Procurement, Inventory, Finance, Human Resources).
2. **Context sidebar**: Deep navigational trees, collapsible folders, and saved view bookmarks.
3. **Top bar**: Global command palette trigger, notification bell, and user profile switcher.
4. **Canvas**: Main content region with dynamic page headers and breadcrumbs.

---

## Complex forms (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/complex-forms)

Architecture for multi-section data entry, validation, and unsaved changes.

# Complex forms

Enterprise procurement, invoicing, and inventory intake require structured data collection spanning dozens of interrelated fields. The complex forms pattern orchestrates `FormLayout`, `Field`, input groups, and validation feedback into a coherent operator experience.

## Design principles

- **Sectional grouping**: Divide extensive forms into logical cards or accordion steps to reduce visual fatigue.
- **Immediate validation**: Validate fields on blur and on submit, displaying inline errors via `FieldError` linked with `aria-describedby`.
- **Dirty state protection**: Track form dirty state and warn operators before navigating away from incomplete transactions.

---

## Data management (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/data-management)

Patterns for enterprise data tables, batch actions, and filtering.

# Data management

High-volume operations at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd involve browsing, filtering, and updating thousands of shipment records and customer accounts. The data management pattern defines how `DataTable`, `Pagination`, search bars, and batch action toolbars collaborate.

## Key considerations

- **Server-driven state**: Sorting, pagination, and multi-field filtering query the backend directly, preserving URL search parameters for link sharing.
- **Batch execution**: Selection toolbars appear upon selecting records, allowing bulk state transitions (e.g. "Approve selected", "Export to CSV").
- **Responsive fallback**: On narrow mobile viewports, tables adapt into card lists or horizontally scrollable containers with pinned identity columns.

---

## Patterns (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/patterns/index)

Reusable composition recipes for enterprise application architectures.

# Patterns

Patterns document established combinations of primitives and widgets that resolve recurrent enterprise challenges at Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd. Rather than prescribing rigid page templates, patterns offer composable blueprints for forms, data tables, and application shells.

## Core patterns

- **Complex forms**: Multi-section data entry, conditional validation with Zod, unsaved changes detection, and accessible error summaries.
- **Data management**: High-density server tables, compound filtering drawers, batch selection workflows, and export pipelines.
- **Application shell**: Responsive dual-tier navigation, persistent command bars, collapsible sidebars, and contextual breadcrumbs.

## Contributing (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/contributing)

Development guidelines, code standards, and PR submission workflows.

# Contributing

Contributions to `@innostes/ui` are welcome from engineering teams across Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd. This guide outlines local environment setup, testing requirements, and quality checks required before submitting pull requests.

## Workflow

1. **Monorepo setup**: Clone the repository and install dependencies with `pnpm install`.
2. **Component development**: Implement new primitives in `packages/ui/src/` adhering strictly to Base UI conventions and British English TSDoc.
3. **Automated verification**: Run uncached quality gates before raising a pull request:
   ```bash
   pnpm nx run-many -t test typecheck build -p ui --skip-nx-cache
   pnpm nx run landing:docs-check
   ```
4. **Documentation**: Every new component requires complete documentation adhering to the component template.

## API Conventions (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/conventions)

The rules every innostes UI component follows, so you can guess the API.

Learn these once and every component works the way you expect.

## Composition

Components with several parts are **flat named exports**, not namespaces:

```tsx
import { Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogContent, DialogTitle } from '@innostes/ui';
```

Everything is exported from the package root. Imports are tree-shaken: you only ship what you use.


## Customization

innostes UI provides several mechanisms for customization, from global theming to pinpoint overrides.

### 1. Design tokens

Design tokens are CSS custom properties defined in `packages/ui/tailwind/theme.css`. Changing a token re-themes every component that uses it automatically across both light and dark modes.

```css
/* Change the primary colour and fluid type scale globally */
@theme {
  --color-primary: var(--color-indigo-600);
  --text-display: clamp(2rem, 1.5rem + 2.5vw, 3rem);
}
```

### 2. CSS variables for sizing

Certain dimensions are exposed as CSS variables rather than semantic tokens. This allows you to set them via component props or override them in CSS.

```tsx
// Set via prop (writes the CSS variable inline)
<SidebarProvider width="20rem">
  <Sidebar />
</SidebarProvider>
```

```css
/* Or override globally in your CSS */
:root {
  --sidebar-width: 20rem;
  --sidebar-width-icon: 4rem;
  --sidebar-width-mobile: min(20rem, 85vw);
  --app-rail-width: 5rem;
  --top-bar-height: 4.5rem;
}
```

### 3. `className`

Like any React component, the plain `className` prop acts as a Tailwind escape hatch on the component's root element. It is merged using `tailwind-merge`, so your classes win over internal defaults.

```tsx
<Button className="rounded-full shadow-lg">Save</Button>
```

### 4. `classNames` (multi-part overrides)

For complex components with multiple parts, the `classNames` prop (using `SlotClassNames<Slot>`) allows you to override styles for specific internal slots.

Every styled element carries a `data-slot` attribute. Values passed to `classNames` are merged last, resolving conflicts via Tailwind.

```tsx
<MetricCard
  label="Revenue"
  value="$12,000"
  classNames={{
    root: 'border-blue-200',
    value: 'text-blue-700 font-serif'
  }}
/>
```

The following components support the `classNames` prop:
`ActionList`, `ActivityFeed`, `AppSwitcher`, `CommandPalette`, `DataTable`, `DonutChart`, `EmptyState`, `EntityList`, `MetricCard`, `Notifications`, `PageHeader`, `QuickActions`, `Stepper`, `UserMenu`, `WelcomeBanner`, `WidgetCard`.

### 5. `render` prop (polymorphism)

Via Base UI's `useRender`/`mergeProps`, you can swap the underlying element or component entirely while keeping the component's behavior and ARIA attributes intact.

```tsx
// Renders the button as a Next.js Link
<Button render={<Link href="/settings" />} nativeButton={false}>
  Settings
</Button>
```

## Responsiveness

### 1. Fluid typography

Instead of fixed sizes or viewport breakpoints, innostes UI uses `clamp()`-based fluid typography for smooth scaling.

```css
/* Fluid type automatically scales based on viewport width */
--text-heading: clamp(1.375rem, 1.2rem + 0.75vw, 1.875rem);
```

### 2. Container queries

For component-level responsiveness, innostes UI relies on CSS container queries (`@container`, `@max-*`) rather than viewport breakpoints. This is crucial because components often live inside sidebars or panels and need to respond to their *available space*, not the overall screen size.

```tsx
// DataTable switches to stack mode based on its container's width, not the screen width
<DataTable responsive="stack" data={data} columns={columns} />
```

Components utilizing container queries include `DataTable`, `Stepper`, and `WelcomeBanner`.

## Controlled and uncontrolled

Every stateful component works both ways, using React's naming:

| Uncontrolled | Controlled | Callback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultValue` | `value` | `onValueChange` |
| `defaultOpen` | `open` | `onOpenChange` |
| `defaultChecked` | `checked` | `onCheckedChange` |
| `defaultPressed` | `pressed` | `onPressedChange` |

Callbacks receive the new value first, then an `eventDetails` object (with `reason` and `event`).

## Styling

- **`className`** is merged with `tailwind-merge`, so your classes win over ours.
  On interactive parts it can also be a function of the component state:
  `className={({ disabled }) => (disabled ? 'opacity-30' : undefined)}`.
- **`data-slot`** names every part (`data-slot="dialog-content"`), so you can target parts from CSS
  or a parent: `[&_[data-slot=card-title]]:text-lg`.
- **State attributes** come from Base UI: `data-open`, `data-checked`, `data-disabled`,
  `data-highlighted`, `data-invalid`, … Style states with Tailwind's `data-*:` variants.
- **Variant helpers** (`buttonVariants`, `badgeVariants`, `inputVariants`, `toggleVariants`) give you
  the classes without the component, e.g. for router links. They're server-safe.

## Rendering another element

Parts built on Base UI take a `render` prop to change the element or compose with your own:

```tsx
<Button render={<Link href="/orders" />} nativeButton={false}>Orders</Button>
<DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Edit</DialogTrigger>
```

Our props and handlers are merged into the element you pass.

## Refs

Every component forwards `ref` to its root element with `forwardRef`, so refs work the same on
React 17, 18 and 19.

## Server Components

Interactive components ship with `"use client"`, so you can import them into Server Components.
Pure helpers (`cn`, `buttonVariants`, `getPaginationRange`, …) don't, and work on the server.

## Sizes

Controls share one size scale so they line up in a row:

| Size | Height | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sm` | 32px | Dense tables, toolbars |
| `md` | 40px | Default |
| `lg` | 48px | Marketing pages, touch-first screens |

## Accessibility

- Keyboard support and ARIA come from Base UI, which follows the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices.
- Icon-only controls require an `aria-label`. The docs for each component list what you must provide.
- Every component is tested for its roles and keyboard behaviour.

## Versioning

innostes UI follows [semantic versioning](https://semver.org). Breaking changes only happen in major
versions and are listed in the changelog with a migration note.

---

## FAQ (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/faq)

Frequently asked questions regarding @innostes/ui installation, theming, and usage.

# Frequently asked questions

Common questions and answers regarding `@innostes/ui` integration and enterprise usage.

## General

### How does innostes UI differ from standard Tailwind component libraries?

`@innostes/ui` is built directly on Base UI unstyled primitives, ensuring full WAI-ARIA compliance, roving focus management, and keyboard accessibility by default. Tailwind CSS v4 provides token-based styling rather than arbitrary utility classes.

### Can I use innostes UI with React 17 or React 18?

Yes. The package is thoroughly tested and verified across React 17, React 18, and React 19 runtimes using dedicated test matrices in our CI pipeline.

### Does the library support dark mode?

Yes. All components consume OKLCH semantic variables that dynamically adjust when toggling between `.light` and `.dark` class names or `data-theme` attributes on the root container.

## Migration guides (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/migration)

Upgrade instructions and breaking change migrations between major versions.

# Migration guides

Detailed upgrade procedures and codemod instructions for transitioning across major `@innostes/ui` releases.

## Upgrading to 0.1.0

The initial enterprise overhaul release normalizes component properties and aligns layout behaviors with Base UI conventions:

- **Breadcrumb**: Resolved false-positive active state warnings; root items now default to `href` links whilst terminal items omit anchors.
- **Progress and Meter**: Value bounds are now strictly clamped between 0 and 100, accepting explicit `aria-valuetext` formatters.
- **Dialog and Sheet**: Replaced directional string literals with logical `side="start" | "end"` positioning properties.
- **RichTextEditor**: Added explicit `invalid` boolean prop for uniform validation integration inside `<Field>`.

## Security (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/security)

Security practices, vulnerability reporting, and dependency auditing.

# Security

Security is foundational to the development lifecycle of `@innostes/ui`. Because the library runs in mission-critical ERP environments handling sensitive business and financial data, all components undergo continuous security review.

## Reporting vulnerabilities

If you discover a potential security vulnerability within `@innostes/ui` or associated tooling, please report it privately:

- Send vulnerability disclosures directly to `security@innostes.com`.
- Avoid filing public issues on GitHub for undisclosed security vulnerabilities.
- Provide reproduction steps, package version, and expected impact.

## Dependency auditing

Automated dependency audits execute on every CI run via `pnpm audit`. High or critical severity findings block release pipelines until patches or vendor updates are merged.

---

## Versioning and support (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/resources/versioning)

Semantic versioning policy, release lifecycle, and browser compatibility targets.

# Versioning and support

The `@innostes/ui` package follows Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0). Version numbers adhere to the `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` structure, providing predictable upgrade paths for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's engineering teams.

## Release cadence

- **Patch releases** (`0.1.x`): Backwards-compatible bug fixes, security remediations, and performance improvements.
- **Minor releases** (`0.x.0`): Backwards-compatible feature additions, new components, and deprecation notices.
- **Major releases** (`x.0.0`): Breaking changes, major architectural migrations, or minimum React runtime requirement upgrades.

## Supported environments

The library supports modern evergreen desktop and mobile browsers:

- Chromium (Chrome, Edge, Opera) latest 2 major versions.
- Mozilla Firefox latest 2 major versions.
- Apple Safari latest 2 major versions.
- Node.js LTS versions (v20, v22) for SSR and build tooling.

## Theming (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/theming)

Change colours once in your Tailwind theme and every component follows.

Components are styled with **semantic tokens** such as `bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground` or
`border-border`. Each token is a CSS variable with a default from Tailwind's palette.

<ThemingDemo />

## Override tokens

With Tailwind, set any token in your `@theme` block. Anything you leave out keeps its default.

```css title="app/globals.css"
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@innostes/ui/tailwind.css';

@theme {
  --color-primary: var(--color-emerald-600);
  --color-primary-hover: var(--color-emerald-700);
  --radius-md: 0.75rem;
}
```

Because defaults point at Tailwind's palette (`--color-primary` is `--color-blue-600`), changing
your palette also changes the components.

Without Tailwind, set the same CSS variables on `:root`:

```css
:root {
  --color-primary: #16a34a;
  --color-primary-hover: #15803d;
}
```

## Dark mode

Import the dark theme. It switches on under a `.dark` class or `data-theme="dark"` on any ancestor,
usually `<html>`, which is what `next-themes` and most theme switchers set.

```css
@import '@innostes/ui/dark.css';
```

To customise it, override tokens inside your own `.dark` block after the import.

## Scoped themes

Tokens are plain CSS variables, so you can re-theme a part of the page, e.g. a white-label area:

```tsx
<section style={{ '--color-primary': 'var(--color-violet-600)' } as React.CSSProperties}>
  <Button>Uses violet</Button>
</section>
```

## Tokens

| Token | Default | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `background` / `foreground` | white / zinc-950 | Page surface and text |
| `card` / `card-foreground` | white / zinc-950 | Cards, tables, sidebar |
| `popover` / `popover-foreground` | white / zinc-950 | Menus, dialogs, popovers, toasts |
| `primary` (`-hover`, `-foreground`) | blue-600 (blue-700, white) | Main actions, selection, focus |
| `secondary` (`-hover`, `-foreground`) | zinc-100 (zinc-200, zinc-900) | Secondary actions |
| `muted` / `muted-foreground` | zinc-100 / zinc-500 | Subtle backgrounds, help text |
| `accent` / `accent-foreground` | zinc-100 / zinc-900 | Hovered and highlighted items |
| `destructive` (`-hover`, `-foreground`) | red-600 (red-700, white) | Dangerous actions, errors |
| `success` / `success-foreground` | emerald-600 / white | Positive status |
| `warning` / `warning-foreground` | amber-500 / amber-950 | Caution status |
| `info` / `info-foreground` | sky-600 / white | Neutral status |
| `border` | zinc-200 | Dividers and outlines |
| `input` | zinc-300 | Form control borders |
| `ring` | blue-500 | Focus outlines |
| `overlay` | black / 40% | Backdrop behind dialogs |

Each token is a colour variable: `--color-<token>`, used as `bg-<token>`, `text-<token>`,
`border-<token>` and so on. Sizes, radius and fonts use Tailwind's standard tokens
(`--spacing`, `--radius-md`, `--text-sm`, …).

---

## App Switcher (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/app-switcher)

A rich popover menu designed for the ECOSYSTEM module launcher, featuring grouped apps, descriptions, icons, and built-in search functionality.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/app-switcher/basic" align="center" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import { AppSwitcher } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

The `AppSwitcher` is primarily used in the top bar as a way to navigate between large, distinct parts of an ecosystem (e.g., switching from the HRMS module to the ERP module).

It accepts an array of `sections`, where each section contains a list of `apps`.

```tsx
function TopNavigation() {
  const sections = [
    {
      label: 'Modules',
      apps: [
        {
          id: 'erp',
          name: 'ERP',
          description: 'Business operations',
          icon: <BuildingIcon />,
          tone: 'chart-1',
          href: '/erp'
        },
        {
          id: 'hrms',
          name: 'HRMS',
          description: 'People & HR',
          icon: <UsersIcon />,
          tone: 'chart-3',
          href: '/hrms'
        },
      ]
    },
  ];

  return <AppSwitcher value="hrms" sections={sections} />;
}
```

### Routing

You can handle navigation in three ways:

1. Provide an `href` to each app. The item will render as an `<a>` tag.
2. Provide a `render` element (e.g., `render={<Link href="/hrms" />}`). The component will merge its props into your custom link component.
3. Use the controlled `value` and `onValueChange` props to navigate programmatically when an app is selected.

### Search

The component automatically includes a search input if there are more than 6 applications provided across all sections. You can manually force it to show or hide by setting the `searchable` boolean prop.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['AppSwitcher']} />

---

## Change Log (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/change-log)

An audit trail with field-level before and after values, notes and day groups.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/change-log/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { ChangeLog } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

Map your audit records to entries, newest first:

```tsx
<ChangeLog
  groupByDay
  entries={audit.map((a) => ({
    id: a.id,
    actor: a.user.name,
    action: a.summary, // "updated the invoice"
    time: new Date(a.at),
    changes: a.diff.map((d) => ({ field: d.label, from: d.old, to: d.new })),
    note: a.comment,
  }))}
/>
```

- `from` and `to` take any content, e.g. status badges. Empty values show `emptyValue` (default "—").
- Built on `ActivityFeed`'s timeline, so it takes the same `groupByDay`, `locale` and `now` props. Use `ActivityFeed` for event streams without field changes.

## Accessibility

Changes are a description list; old values use `<del>` and new values `<ins>`, with hidden "from" / "to" labels (`diffLabels` to translate).

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['ChangeLog']} />

---

## Widgets (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/index)

High-level business components combining multiple primitives for enterprise ERP patterns.

import { CategoryGrid } from '@/components/docs/category-grid';

# Widgets

Widgets are domain-ready, composite enterprise components designed specifically for Northwind Traders Pvt Ltd's ERP operations. From role-based access matrixes to drag-and-drop Kanban logistics boards, widgets assemble primitives into production-ready business blocks.

## Components

<CategoryGrid category="widgets" />

## Usage guidelines

- **Business logic separation**: Widgets encapsulate UI interactions and visual states while accepting pure data props and callback handlers for business operations.
- **Data density**: Widgets support compact display modes to present high-density business intelligence without visual clutter.
- **Touch and keyboard**: All widgets include accessible touch targets and keyboard alternatives for mouse-intensive operations.

---

## Kanban Board (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/kanban-board)

Pipelines, deals, tickets and approval stages, with drag and drop, keyboard moves and WIP limits.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/kanban-board/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { KanbanBoard, moveKanbanItem, type KanbanColumn } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

Cards need a string `id`. The board renders the card frame; `renderCard` renders what's inside.

```tsx
<KanbanBoard
  aria-label="Deals"
  value={columns}
  onValueChange={(next, move) => {
    setColumns(next);
    api.updateDealStage(move.itemId, move.toColumnId, move.toIndex);
  }}
  canMove={(move) => !(move.fromColumnId === 'lead' && move.toColumnId === 'won')}
  getItemLabel={(deal) => deal.name}
  renderCard={(deal) => <DealCard deal={deal} />}
  onCardOpen={(deal) => router.push(`/deals/${deal.id}`)}
/>
```

- `onValueChange` gets the new columns and the move (`itemId`, `fromColumnId`, `fromIndex`, `toColumnId`, `toIndex`).
- `canMove` blocks moves, e.g. skipping a required stage.
- `limit` on a column shows `count/limit` and turns red above it.
- `columnActions` adds buttons to column headers.
- `moveKanbanItem(columns, itemId, toColumnId, toIndex)` applies a move to plain data, e.g. for optimistic updates or real-time sync.

Mouse dragging uses native HTML drag and drop, which doesn't work on touch screens. On phones, let people open the card (`onCardOpen`) and change its stage there.

## Accessibility

Drag and drop isn't required. Each card is focusable, and every step is announced:

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Arrows | Move focus between cards and columns |
| Space | Pick up the card, then drop it |
| Arrows (holding) | Move the card up, down or to another column |
| Escape | Cancel the move |
| Enter | `onCardOpen` |

Pass `labels` to translate the instructions and announcements.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['KanbanBoard']} />

---

## Metric Card (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/metric-card)

One component, seven designs: default, compact, sparkline, progress, comparison, split and accent.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/metric-card/variants" align="start" />

## Import

```tsx
import { MetricCard, MetricGrid, MetricDelta } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Choosing a variant

| Variant | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | The standard KPI row: icon, value, trend and comparison. |
| `compact` | Many metrics in little space, e.g. a sidebar or a dense ops dashboard. |
| `accent` | The one or two metrics that matter most on the page. |
| `sparkline` | When the direction over time matters more than one number. |
| `progress` | Progress towards a target: sales quota, budget, OKR. |
| `comparison` | This period next to the previous one, side by side. |
| `split` | One total broken down into a few parts, e.g. attendance by status. |

Use one variant per row so the row lines up.

## Deltas and trends

```tsx
<MetricCard label="Revenue" value="€48,250" delta={0.125} comparison="vs last month" />   // ↑ +12.5% (green)
<MetricCard label="Refund rate" value="1.2%" delta={0.2} upIsGood={false} />              // ↑ +20% (red)
<MetricCard label="Team" value="42" delta="+3 people" />                                  // string, shown as is
```

- A **number** `delta` is a fraction: `0.125` shows as `+12.5%`, formatted for the user's locale.
  Change it with `deltaFormat` (any `Intl.NumberFormat` options).
- A **string** `delta` is shown as is. A leading `+` or `-` sets the arrow.
- `upIsGood={false}` flips the colours for metrics where an increase is bad.
- The arrow is announced to screen readers ("Up", "Down"), so colour isn't the only signal.

## Formatting values

`value` is a `ReactNode`: format it yourself so it matches the rest of your app.

```tsx
const money = new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR', maximumFractionDigits: 0 });
<MetricCard label="Revenue" value={money.format(revenue)} />
```

## Links, menus and loading

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/metric-card/states" align="start" />

- `render={<Link href="/orders" />}` makes the whole card a link (with hover and focus styles).
- `action` adds a control in the corner, e.g. a `DropdownMenu`. (Not with `render`, because a link
  can't contain a button.)
- `loading` shows a skeleton in place of the value and sets `aria-busy`.

## Layout

`MetricGrid` fits as many equal columns as there's room for. Set `minCardWidth` (default `14rem`)
to control when it wraps.

## `MetricDelta` on its own

The coloured trend is exported for tables and lists:

```tsx
<MetricDelta delta={-0.04} upIsGood={false} />
```

`getTrend`, `getSentiment` and `formatDelta` are exported too. They have no React code, so they
work anywhere.

## Customization

Like all innostes UI components, this widget supports overriding styles via `className`, `classNames` (where applicable), and swapping the root element via the `render` prop. See [Conventions](/ui/docs/resources/conventions#customization) for the full customization model.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['MetricCard', 'MetricGrid']} />

---

## Notification Bell (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/notification-bell)

A rich popover component to display recent notifications, relative timestamps, and unread statuses, usually placed in the TopBar.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/notification-bell/basic" align="center" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import { NotificationBell, NotificationList, NotificationItem } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

The `NotificationBell` is primarily used in the top bar. It wraps a trigger and a popover containing a `NotificationList`.

It automatically calculates the unread count based on the `items` provided (items where `read` is falsy or `undefined`), or you can explicitly provide an `unreadCount`.

```tsx
function TopNavigation() {
  const notifications: NotificationItem[] = [
    {
      id: '1',
      title: 'New message from Sarah',
      description: 'Can we review the latest designs?',
      time: new Date(),
      icon: <MessageSquareIcon />,
      tone: 'primary',
      read: false,
    },
    // ...
  ];

  return (
    <NotificationBell
      items={notifications}
      onMarkAllRead={() => markAllRead()}
      viewAll={{ href: '/notifications' }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Notification List

If you need to render the list of notifications outside of the bell popover (for example, on a dedicated full-page notifications view or inside a widget card), you can use the `NotificationList` component directly.

```tsx
<NotificationList
  items={notifications}
  onItemClick={(item) => markRead(item.id)}
/>
```

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['NotificationBell', 'NotificationList']} />

---

## Permission Matrix (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/permission-matrix)

Resources by actions, grouped by module, with row and column "all" toggles.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/permission-matrix/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { PermissionMatrix, permissionKey } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<PermissionMatrix
  aria-label={`Permissions for ${role.name}`}
  actions={[
    { id: 'view', label: 'View' },
    { id: 'edit', label: 'Edit' },
    { id: 'approve', label: 'Approve' },
  ]}
  resources={[
    { id: 'invoices', label: 'Invoices', group: 'Finance' },
    { id: 'payroll', label: 'Payroll', group: 'HR', actions: ['view', 'approve'] },
  ]}
  value={role.permissions}
  onValueChange={(permissions) => save({ ...role, permissions })}
/>
```

- The value is a flat list of `"resource:action"` keys. `permissionKey(resource, action)` builds one.
- `actions` on a resource limits which actions apply; other cells show a dash.
- `group` lists rows under section headings, in the order they first appear.
- `readOnly` shows the permissions without bulk toggles or changes, e.g. for system roles.

## Accessibility

A real `<table>` with row and column headers. Every checkbox is named after its action and resource ("Edit Invoices"); bulk toggles show a mixed state when only some permissions are granted.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['PermissionMatrix']} />

## Sparkline (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/sparkline)

Pure SVG, no chart library, server-safe.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/sparkline/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { Sparkline } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

```tsx
<Sparkline data={[12, 18, 15, 22, 28]} tone="success" label="Orders, last 5 days, rising" />
```

- It fills the width of its container; set the height with `height` (default 40px).
- `area={false}` draws only the line, which suits table cells.
- Without `label` it's decorative and hidden from screen readers. Add a `label` when the trend
  carries information that isn't written next to it.

For full charts with axes and tooltips, use the chart components (coming next).

## Customization

Like all innostes UI components, this widget supports overriding styles via `className`, `classNames` (where applicable), and swapping the root element via the `render` prop. See [Conventions](/ui/docs/resources/conventions#customization) for the full customization model.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['Sparkline']} />

## User Menu (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/user-menu)

A user profile button that opens a dropdown menu. Typically used in the top bar or sidebar footer to access profile settings and sign out.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/user-menu/basic" align="center" className="p-4 sm:p-4" />

## Import

```tsx
import { UserMenu } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

The `UserMenu` provides a consistent trigger showing the user's avatar and details. It wraps a dropdown menu, so you can pass standard `DropdownMenuItem` components as children.

```tsx
function AppHeader() {
  return (
    <UserMenu
      name="Arun Kumar"
      subtitle="Acme Corp"
      email="arun@acme.com"
      avatarSrc={user.photoUrl}
    >
      <DropdownMenuItem>Profile</DropdownMenuItem>
      <DropdownMenuItem>Settings</DropdownMenuItem>
      <DropdownMenuSeparator />
      <DropdownMenuItem variant="destructive" onClick={signOut}>
        Sign out
      </DropdownMenuItem>
    </UserMenu>
  );
}
```

### Avatar fallback

If `avatarSrc` is not provided, the component automatically generates initials based on the `name` prop (e.g., "Arun Kumar" -> "AK"). You can override this behavior by explicitly passing an `initials` string.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['UserMenu']} />

## Widget Card (https://innostes.com/ui/docs/widgets/widget-card)

Header with title, count, actions and "View all", plus built-in loading, empty and error states.

<ComponentPreview name="widgets/widget-card/basic" />

## Import

```tsx
import { WidgetCard } from '@innostes/ui';
```

## Usage

Wrap any dashboard content (a list, a table, a chart) to give it a consistent header and the
three states every data widget needs:

```tsx
const { data, isLoading, error, refetch } = usePendingActions();

<WidgetCard
  title="Pending actions"
  count={data?.length}
  viewAll={{ href: '/approvals' }}
  actions={<PeriodSelect />}
  loading={isLoading}
  error={error ? 'Could not load pending actions.' : undefined}
  onRetry={refetch}
  empty={data?.length === 0}
  emptyState="You're all caught up."
>
  <PendingActionList items={data} />
</WidgetCard>
```

- `viewAll` takes `href`, `onClick` or `render={<Link href="…" />}` for your router.
- `padding="none"` lets tables and charts reach the card edges.
- `count` shows a badge next to the title (`99+` above 99); `countTone` changes its colour.

## Accessibility

- Renders a `<section>` labelled by its title, so screen-reader users can jump between widgets.
- `headingLevel` (default `h2`) keeps the page outline correct.
- Loading sets `aria-busy`; errors use `role="alert"`.

## Customization

Like all innostes UI components, this widget supports overriding styles via `className`, `classNames` (where applicable), and swapping the root element via the `render` prop. See [Conventions](/ui/docs/resources/conventions#customization) for the full customization model.

## API Reference

<ApiTable components={['WidgetCard']} />

---
